commentary: full to start, just a hint of swing to straighten towards off stump. Clipped to the right of mid-on and Rohit is off the mark
pre_text:
10.26 The anthems are done, and we're ready to begin. Will India reclaim the trophy they last won - with consequences that changed the face of cricket - in 2007, or will South Africa lift their first World Cup? We are about to find out. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli will open for India, as always, and Marco Jansen has the new ball. A leg slip is in position, interestingly, as well as a slip. Will Jansen get this new ball to swing into the right-hander? Left-arm over.



10.21am Barbados Prime Minister Mia Mottley and Chris Gayle bring out the trophy, and the two teams follow them out for the national anthems.

Mandeep: "Why time is so slow now? It just feeling by me or anyone else feel same."

RG: "An ardent Rahul Dravid fan, and a lifetime RSA fan, while being a hardcore Indian. Whom do I support? Will I be more happy or sad today? "

Suryakumar Yadav: "Playing in the final is not easy. Easy to say it's just another game, there is pressure. But if there is no pressure, there is no fun. Excited by my role. Have always enjoyed it. Wind direction plays a big role here. Know what my strengths are and back myself. Back of the mind, it feels really good to know I have a good record against SA but you have to start afresh on the day. (Conversations last night) Sleep well, stay fresh, stay hydrated (laughs)."

Boomerang : "About Kettleborough and India and the supposed curse: all it really shows is that both have been amongst the best for a very long time now. "

AJ: "Apart from the CT17 final, all the finals that India have lost they have batted first. Let's see how things unfold here." -- I'm guessing you mean all the recent finals they've lost. Some of us can never forget 2003...

Subhayan: "As an Indian is it controversial to say 'whoever wins today, I will be happy'? Have to submit that one part of the heart is rooting for the team who has faced so much dissappointment over years. "

Andrew Leckonby: "6 different finalists in the last 3 T20 World cups! That's so unlike cricket but surely another positive about T20."

SJ: "This is probably the first time 5 left arm spinners are playing in a match." -- And a rare instance of two left-arm wristspinners too.

10.00am Here we go, here we go. Aiden Markram flips the coin at the Kensington Oval, and Rohit Sharma calls tails. India will bat first. "It's just about understanding the individual role, keep calm, and play like it's an international match against a top team. Just stay calm and composed. South Africa have played really good cricket in this tournament, we have played really good cricket too, two quality teams." India are unchanged.

Markram says he would have liked to bat first too. "Looks pretty dry" is his assessment of the pitch. "At times probably not been at our best, but we've found a way to win. Today we're striving for that perfect game, even if perfect is not attainable. It's a fantastic opportunity, no pressure for us, we've never been in a final. You can't win a trophy if you aren't in the final." South Africa are unchanged too.

India: 1 Rohit Sharma (capt), 2 Virat Kohli, 3 Rishabh Pant (wk), 4 Suryakumar Yadav, 5 Shivam Dube, 6 Hardik Pandya, 7 Axar Patel, 8 Ravindra Jadeja, 9 Arshdeep Singh, 10 Kuldeep Yadav, 11 Jasprit Bumrah.

South Africa: 1 Quinton de Kock (wk), 2 Reeza Hendricks, 3 Aiden Markram (capt), 4 Heinrich Klaasen, 5 David Miller, 6 Tristan Stubbs, 7 Marco Jansen, 8 Keshav Maharaj, 9 Kagiso Rabada, 10 Anrich Nortje, 11 Tabraiz Shamsi.

This is the first time since 2012 that the captain winning the toss has chosen to bat first in a T20 World Cup final. A lot of that has to do with this being a day game, clearly. Ian Bishop said the pitch looked hard during his pitch report, but not a lot of live grass, so perhaps it could get a little drier as it goes along and bring the spinners into play to a greater degree as the match goes on.

deepak: "100th T20I for Pandya. Go well Champ."

ankur baid : "Last dance for Rohit and Kohli together for India in blue shirt." -- Maybe in T20Is, possibly, but I see them playing on for a while in Tests and probably ODIs too. 

9.56am Thanks, Ekanth, and a warm hello to everyone here. Four minutes to go for the toss. Cannot wait!

Azweer: "In 7 out of 8 T20 World Cup finals, the team which won the Toss had won the game. Will it repeat today too..!!" Yes, you're right Karthik confirms as he prepares to hop on here.

Pitch and conditions: 'All numbers around the weather are in the 30s', says Nasser Hussain, '30 degree centigrade, 30% chance of rain (hope that goes to none), and 30km/hr winds and they're important and they're blowing in the direction of the slightly smaller boundary. This is the central pitch.

Ian Bishop says it's an interesting-looking surface. It's been that way all tournament. It's been rolled a bit but there's no live grass. It's hard to start with, hope the ball comes on to bat nicely. More wickets have fallen to pacers here, which may indicate more bounce. As the game goes on, I wouldn't be surprised if there are footmarks and it grips and slows a bit. The ball hasn't carried as well as it has in St Lucia but pacers have been effective because if you work hard and hit surface, it can be uncomfortable to drive down and play square. Nasser finishes off saying this is a fair pitch which might not have the bounce of St Lucia or the low bounce of Guyana, says he hopes there is even pace and bounce, which is all everyone wants.


9:46am: Time for the Indian players to get into a huddle. An enthusiastic Rohit gives a pep talk and they finish cheerfully. Stubbs, Markram, Klaasen all having a hit. Maharaj has a bowl. Shamsi too. Sign of things to come?

AS: "not a sell out crowd? " Not yet. Building up nicely, buzzing, definitely better than the India semi-final


Jan: "Bumrah marking his runup, so he will be in the team!!!" lol


9:32am Here's Monga, "Bumrah is marking his run, and gets a pat on his back. Sanjana Ganesan, a media professional who is working on the field herself and is Bumrah's wife, gives him a last-minute hug to wish him luck." South Africa's players get in a huddle minutes later. Markram has a chat, they disperse calmly.

Rim: "So pitch supporting SA pacers more than India's. Will be interesting to see if both teams replace one spinner with seamer. Advantage SA with kind of pace attack they have." Yeah, Coetzee sounds like a good pick. That'll mean Shamsi goes out?

sam: "how is pitch on the rating between highway and paddy field?" Closer to highway. Here's a bit from Nasser Hussain's report:



Sujatha : "This is very harsh world , with the advent of social media. The losing team is sure to get bashings on social media. One would request all the bashing population to be empathetic with the losing side. Both teams have been nothing short of brilliant" Yeah, as Alagappan Muthu, who's started the Live Blog, wrote rather eloquently in the match preview, 'both India and South Africa should be reminded that they are excellent teams and exceptional people. They should both be able to share their love with family. Toast their time with colleagues. Chase after their children. Enjoy the compassion of their fans. If any of that is contingent on the colour of the medal around their necks, we're doing something really wrong.'

JJ: "If both days are washed out, will India and South Africa share the trophy?" Yes, if the weather prevents the match from being completed even on the reserve day, both teams shall be declared joint-winners, but that (thankfully) seems like it won't be the case.

Pranav: "@Ekanth beautiful plug of sun is shining!! That was around the time I started following cricket, when this was the opening sequence of india's tour of WI, probably 2004/05" Cheers, 2006 definitely, but yeah a mid-2000s staple

AHN from Kohat: "Albeit a Pakistani, I'm all for India today. It's just the way it is folks. "

Dilan K: "@Swathi and @Bishnoi - As a Srilankan, Andrew F Fernando is the only thing going well for us in the cricket world. Amazing writing brother, that Rashid article was next level. " Thanks on his behalf, will pass it on to him


9:20am: "Pitch is being rolled at the moment, says Matt. "Some blues shirts starting to filter into the stands." It will be the centre-wicket. 40 minutes away from the toss, and the sights are pristine. Sun is shining, weather is sweet.

Yogesh from NJ: "What is the "Richard Kettleborough jinx"?  Can I apply it as a reverse jinx, by saying that it'll work today and stop India?" He'd officiated in some capacity in eight of the knockout games India have lost in the last ten years. Don't know about reverse jinx

Monga reminds that the Scotland-England game happened here which was high-scoring. India-Afghanistan too, was here, and India made 180, which was said to be 10-15 above par.

'Shamsi is marking his run', informs Monga. 'I expect no change in either side'

8:55am The Indian team has arrived at the ground. A few fans outside the fence with phones out recording. The South African players are in and training. Reeza Hendricks is around for a pre-match interview. Music's playing, and it's just as sunny still. 'Yet to see her myself but the word is that Rihanna is here...' informs Matt Roller.

"Chasing becomes a bit harder when it comes to final or sf in this format," theorises ShahSafeer, "but we all know whoever wins the toss will go for chasing which suggests losing the toss would be a better thing to begin with for either of two captains. At least they'll start the proceeding without thinking too much about what they actually should've gone with, bat or ball! "


swathi: "@Bishnoi - Totally agree. The Rashid article bought a slight tear in my eye at the end. These are articles that makes rabid fans like me (who easily sit at home and criticize) remember that players are humans as well."

Sowmya : "Hope SA don't do the mistake that Bangladesh, Australia and England did against India -Win the toss and choose to chase " Don't think chasing will be as bad

Dublin Joe: "Barbados webcams if anyone wants to check the weather out" Thanks for the link. It's a pretty cool feature actually. Here's the one at Pebble beach, which Google Maps says is about 5km away

Sam: "Can India break the Richard Kettleborough jinx?"


ashish: "Shamsi and Maharaj will create real issues yet again for India as they will slow down against the spinners. "

The guy: "What are chances of match starting late or even tomorrow due to weather? I wish it pospones to tomorrow " Toss is likely to happen on time. 10am passing shower is what Monga's forecast said, but the whole match happening today seems almost certain.




Cheers, Suds. It's just 8:40am at Barbados but might as well be 11 as it's so bright. Perfect for one of these teams to end their trophy-drought. Boy, so many narratives around that but as some of the pieces linked below demonstrate, they can be dealt with maturity. Lots to appreciate, lots to look forward to and lots to chat about. Thanks for all the comments btw, keep em coming.

Sudhir: "Not sure what app Sidharth Monga has but multiple radars from my end show no rain for the near future. Fingers crossed. These two wonderful teams with great, hard working and truly nice players deserve a bright on time start and a beautiful day for having one of the best days of their lives. Currently 34000 ft heading South from Boston, for the next few hours. Cricinfo is all that I have. Thank you. " Thanks for tuning in, Sudhir. Also, Monga had said, "My phone seems to suggest only one passing shower at 10 and nothing else through the day." Also, he's made the ground and there are a few folks outside the ground.

Vaneez : "All the teams Klassen has represented in his last three finals in IPL,SA20,MLC have lost , wonder if the streak can end today."

Vikram : "Dube has to give way for Jaiswal or Samson." Might not be that bad a call but Dube fits well in India's plan where the top three attack and then he comes in as a spin basher. There was a bit of criticism last game around him coming too far down. But looking back, England had bowled most of their overs from spinners and Hardik coming early gave him a bit of time. But again, think it'll be unlikely.

Jay: "talking about wholesale changes, India should play Jaiswal for Kohli and Samson for Dube! bold calls but that will make for a very strong team!" Um, no. Gotta agree with Suds on this one

Right then, time for me to hand over the reins to Ekanth, who's all set with his evening coffee!




8:30am A tall, left-arm fast bowler, swinging it into the right-hand India batter. Don't want to think it as an India fan, would you? Marco Jansen is just the kind of bowler that you would want in your team in a crunch game against India. But he has wild fluctuations in his returns in "big match". Sidharth Monga explores the returns of one of South Africa's key players, with Shiva Jayaraman's stats inputs.

Bishnoi: "Feature Article " The Rashid Phenom.." by Andrew Fidel Fernando also deserves special acknowledgement. The link and article will always be saved in our laptops and minds alike. Fantastic Team"

Suresh: "India should bring in Jaiswal/ Samson in place of Dube and let them open with Rohit. Kohli at 3 and Pant down the order. This will surprise SA." Hard to see such wholesale changes, tbh...

Kiernan: "5 lifelong and long-suffering Proteaa fans are gathered and ready for the final we have been dreaming off. A QDK and Nortje masterclass is first prize, but ready for a nail biter and pain. Cricket Chat, unite!"

Pokhrel: "A great game of cricket waiting for neutral fans. Want to root for South Africa for what they have gone through in the last 25 years since that 1999 world cup semi final with Australia. Hope they beat their demons and get the title. "




8:10am It is the first men's T20 World Cup final since 2010 that will be played in day time. All of India's matches have been day games, while South Africa have also played three in the day. India played Afghanistan at the Kensington Oval while the title-clash will be South Africa's first at this venue in this competition. What are some of the tactics to keep an eye on, then? Nagraj Gollapudi, with help from S Rajesh and Shiva Jayaraman, looks at possible areas where the game could be decided.




Babu: "I actually wish it rains and the trophy gets shared. Both deserving." You must be in the minority here, surely Babu! :D 

Deepak: "Kindly convey my regards to Sid Monga. That heartbreak article is a true masterpiece !"

Matthew: "What's QdK doing after this? Is he retiring from international cricket altogether, or has he yet to say? Would be a shame if he finishes without a senior world title IMO, he's been a great player. " Should be the it but you never know

Mohit: "Match is never complete without cricinfo feed. Even I have watched almost all games on TV, I have always stayed tuned with the commentary. Thanks for bringing the paper book reading type feel back in our hectic lifestyles. #CricInfoFan"





7:50am Sidharth Monga's weather app tells him that we can expect a passing shower around 10am local time, and nothing much apart from that. Let's hope his app is right. *Fingers crossed*

Rahul Dravid and Rohit Sharma have a shot at redemption, having lost the World Cup final at home last year. This will be Dravid's last game as India's coach, and what the road ahead is like for Rohit, the T20I captain, is anybody's guess. On the other hand, South Africa have had a string of heartbreaks in men's World Cups in the past. But they would have had little time to brood over them, much like India, because of the short turnaround plus the travel between the matches. Which of the teams will be able to cross the final hurdle today?

Bharat Mulchand: "I have been invited to watch the match about 1.5 hours away.  I don't want to drive there only to find out that the game is postponed to tomorrow.  What is the likely that the game will begin on time today?" Going by the word from Barbados, we should have an on-time start, as of now. Still over a couple of hours away, you see


Ram: "Nervously waiting for the start and thought of checking weather. Thankfully Cricinfo updates has me calming down a bit."

Jay: "never thought I would be here following Cricinfo commentary 3 hours before the game starts! @Amit also hoping for a Kohli special for possibly his last T20 World Cup game! He needs to play down the ground and not try too hard to hit sixes!!" Have most of y'all assumed this to be Kohli's last T20WC, without it yet coming from the horse's mouth?

Ravish: "I really hope and wish this game gives us a glimpse into how two good teams play true cricket. A game of the gentlemen without the bullying and word wars. I want the kids watching to know how a game of cricket should be played and what better teams to do that. "

juga: "@gibran: you didn't miss much. the sprint was a bit of a let down except for the tussle between lando and max where piastri quite opportunistically pulled off an overtake on lando on the outside for p2"





7:30am What's it like in South Africa ahead of their big cricket day? Firdose Moonda has this to say: "It is very, very quiet in Cape Town. It's the middle of school holidays and loads of people seem to be away or indoors. There's a wind picking up here as well, so the outdoor areas are pretty empty. It's almost a sense that people are too nervous to do too much. Collective breath holding. Word from Joburg is that the fan park at the Wanderers is gong to be vibing. Of course, the Highveld gets icy in the evenings and temperatures will drop as soon as the sun sets around 5.30pm. so an hour into the scheduled start of the match, so it will be interesting to see how many people stay for the full game, especially if there are delays. Overall, South Africa is trying its best not to show how important this is. And for lolz, I spoke to a guy at a store yesterday and and asked him if we knew South Africa were in a World Cup final and he said: 'Oh, is that like one Brazil play. I stopped watching sport in 2010!'"

Gibran: "I woke up an hour late for an F1 race and missed it, but seeing this feed means that waking up at 6am wasn't all completely worthless"

Amit : "Excited for the day and hoping Kohli back in form for the final. Go India!!" 




7:20am A bit of #WeatherWatch from Matt Roller, who is up and about in Bridgetown. He says that there is no rain right now but just a bit of breeze, approximately 4kms away from the ground. There was a lot of rain overnight.

Naveena: "what are you doing here, Suds? should you not be in Chennai?" Srinidhi Ramanujam and Sruthi Ravindranath are our eyes and ears at Chepauk, reporting on the game and dishing out some superb match pieces.

Talkative_intro: "Got up at 6 to complete my studies before the match starts. Resisted but had to check here for the weather forecast. Did not realize that a side benefit could be to become (potentially) the 1st published comment on a hopefully Epic and historic day for Indian cricket. "




7:10am What does the South Africa men's team reaching their first World Cup final mean for a passionate country like theirs? "A men's team in a cricket World Cup final means we are rising, relevant and ready to show the world that sometimes, even in the briefest of moments, shared success is possible. But for once, we're not screaming about it. We're holding our breath, because cricket has not given cause for much else. The disappointments of seven World Cup semi-finals defeats is one reason that South Africans are cautious when it comes to cricket, but there are others," writes Firdose Moonda in 'For South Africa, and those who know what they know'.

Paul Wesley: "As an Indian fan who also supports SA over the years, I have wished for many years for this moment. India Vs SA in a WorldCup final. But now that is here, it's stomach churning. I feel I am gonna be sad unless it ends in a tie. I have realized that, an Indian win will give me joy but a SA victory will give me peace. "

Jay: "As Sidharth Monga has duly marked, both teams duly deserve this title! Best wishes for the both! Hope to see a great match! May the best team wins!"

Wajid Jawaid : "Given South Africa's greater heartbreaks in world tournaments, I think most neutrals would be favouring them today. But then India has millions of followers anyway. I believe today's fan support would be somewhat equal. You may run a poll later to confirm! "

Manish: "Excited to see the comma open early, yay! Would India be tempted to bring in third seamer in this ground favoring seamers? But would they risk leaving Kuldeep out?" Hard to see them tweak their side, Manish





6:50am The Kensington Oval in Barbados has been a key presence in a few of India and South Africa's heartbreaks historically. In World Cups, too, the finalists have endured multiple disappointments. Like India, who finished runners-up in the ODI version at home last year. Or South Africa, who have cleared the semi-final hurdle for the first time in men's World Cups. 

Both teams are unbeaten and have played the best cricket in the conditions on offer. And yet, they will have to live with the reactions of what happens in the final tonight. "That's how it is. It is a fact of life the participants appreciate more than anyone else. For they must live with it. They must play it like any other game but know that it is not seen as that. They must not admit the role luck can play. Yet compulsively they must follow same routines," writes Sidharth Monga in 'Heartbreak or glory, India and South Africa are already winners'.

chetan Patel: "its would be midnight here in Australia by the time the match starts! Thank you Cricinfo for starting the news feed nice and early."





6:30am Open the windows. Feel the air. Let it flow in. Soak it all. Do you feel it? It's Saturday, baby! It's not just any other day, it's #T20WorldCup 2024 final day! 

After four weeks of competitive cricket of different kinds, in the USA and West Indies, we are in Bridgetown, Barbados. India and South Africa, both teams unbeaten, take on one another; one in search of their first ICC title in a decade, and the other, their first-ever world championship title. Al Muthu lays out the bare bones of this contest in his preview.

Hello and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's coverage of the title-clash, wherever you are joining from. It's a big day, a lot of you eager to know what's happening - with the weather as well as the build-up, at the Kensington Oval in Barbados. So we are here nice and early, to feed you updates drip by drip (and I am not referencing the weather here, I swear). Sit back, relax and do chime in with your views!

commentary: and a four first ball for Kohli! Gets a nice, juicy, wide half-volley first up, and he reaches out and meets it with a slightly open face to place it between backward point and cover point
back-to-back fours, and back-to-back freebies from Jansen. Another half-volley, but this one swings into Kohli's pads, and he clips it away neatly to the right of the man at midwicket
another half-volley, just outside off this time, and Kohli gets a nice stride forward, bends his front knee to get his weight into the ball, and plays a checked drive betwen cover and mid-off
good length for the first time in this over, slanting across into the corridor, and immediately there's some carry, de Kock collecting just above his head after Kohli leaves it alone

another half-volley, close to off stump, and Kohli drives straight this time, between the stumps and the non-striker, and both mid-on and mid-off give chase but neither can catch up with the ball, though Nortje, running from mid-on, gets close enough to attempt a sliding save
just a touch back of a length, not a lot of width, but Rohit makes himself room to try and cut. A bit of extra bounce, a thick edge, and it flies away into the big gap between slip and backward point
pre_text: That was the most expensive first over in a T20 World Cup final. Spin from the other end, it's Keshav Maharaj with a slip in place. Left-arm around.

commentary: India are absolutely flying here. On the shorter side of a length, and the line is outside off, and Rohit spots the line early and brings out the reverse-sweep, slaps it away behind backward point
tightens his line, good length on off stump, defended to short extra-cover

gone, what a catch this is from Klaasen! Rohit  continues to try and put pressure on Maharaj. Floated up slow outside off stump - 77kph - and he stretches out to sweep. Middles it, but doesn't really smash it, because he's reaching for the ball - ends up hitting it in the air to the left of square leg, where Klaasen takes a good, low diving catch two-handed
dismissal: RG Sharma c Klaasen b Maharaj 9 (7m 5b 2x4 0x6) SR: 180

commentary: length ball outside off, presses forward and dabs towards backward point
pre_text: In walks Rishabh Pant. A big moment that he's playing this World Cup final at all, after the grave events of December 2022. Over the wicket.

commentary: is that two wickets in the over for Maharaj? Two wickets off the sweep? South Africa think so. The umpires are checking for a bump ball. Goes for the sweep against a very full ball, and ends up meeting it on the full, in fact, outside off. And he's a goner. Straight up in the air off the top edge of the toe end, and it balloons up behind him to de Kock. What a turnaround in the space of three balls, after India had run away to a flier
dismissal: RR Pant c †de Kock b Maharaj 0 (2m 2b 0x4 0x6) SR: 0

commentary: back of a length outside off, and steep bounce through to the keeper after Kohli leaves alone
pre_text: Suryakumar Yadav is in at No. 4. It will be interesting to see how India, and especially Virat Kohli, react to those two wickets.  Kagiso Rabada comes on.

commentary: length ball close to off stump, defended into the point region
fullish, angling in towards off stump, clipped to short midwicket
back of a length outside off, opens his bat face to dab to the left of point
pre_text: Abhijeet: "Rohit does it again. Successful in other games failure in finals. His super aggression doing more harm to the team than the good." -- What a wonderful thing hindsight is. A strategy is obviously good when it works, and obviously bad when it doesn't.

commentary: hard length, straightens a touch towards the top of off, with a bit of extra bounce, squared up slightly while defending to short cover

ooooh, just clears mid-on! Could be one of those sliding-doors moments. Length ball, hits the pitch hard, angling in towards off stump, and SKY goes for the wristy whip over mid-on, but doesn't middle it - the ball hit the bat pretty high up - and it loops up over mid-on, for a moment appearing catchable as the fielder turns around and begins to give chase, but the over-the-shoulder ball doesn't quite land within range
tossed up wide of off, driven with a wristy slap to the left of long-off
quicker, straightens sharply on an off-stump line, squares up a little while defending off the back foot
similar ball, but this time Kohli is right behind it to defend into the covers
short, wide, slapped. Just sits up and Kohli stands up and whacks it away to the left of cover
drifts in towards middle and leg, clipped to backward square leg
length ball close to off stump, goes deep in his crease and cuts to point
length ball outside off, presses forward and guides to deep third
pre_text:
Rabada continues.

Since January 2023, Maharaj had gone for 143 runs in 114 powerplay deliveries, with an economy of 7.52, and picked up six wickets in this phase. That was coming into this game. Make that 8 wickets now.

commentary: on the fuller side of a length, close to off stump, punched with a straight bat to the left of mid-off

three down, and Rabada gets a huuuge wicket. Again, not necessarily a wicket-taking ball, and India's aggressive intent - which has served them so well through this tournament - goes against them. Steps across to a back-of-a-length ball angled in towards the stups, and whips it away, but close enough to fine leg for the fielder to move to his left and take a straightforward catch
dismissal: SA Yadav c Klaasen b Rabada 3 (9m 4b 0x4 0x6) SR: 75

commentary: full on the pads, and he puts it away, clips it neatly to the right of the diving square leg fielder
pre_text: For the second time in this tournament, India promote Axar Patel as a bit of a pinch-anchor after losing early wickets. Rabada stays over the wicket.

commentary: full, not quite a half-volley, slanting away from off stump, driven to cover point

slapped away, and backward point misfields. Maybe some bad bounce for the fielder. Shortish, slanting across into the corridor, gets on top of the bounce and hits it firmly down with a horizontal bat. Rolls away past backward point, but deep third moves left swiftly to cut it off
pre_text: Karthik Iyappan: "The celebration from Klaasen shows how important Surya's Wicket is!!"

commentary: full, angling into middle and leg, clipped to deep midwicket
pre_text: Another spinner in the powerplay. Aiden Markram, the offspinner, with the left-hander at the crease. Round the wicket.

commentary: length ball spinning in from outside off, goes back and across to work it to deep midwicket
pre_text: Over the wicket to Kohli, who's had a quiet time against offspin in this World Cup.

commentary: fired into the pads from round the wicket, clipped into the midwicket region. Replay shows that Markram delivered this from well behind the crease
full, close to off stump, too full for elevation. Whipped down to long-on, all along the ground
floated up full on leg stump, whipped to deep midwicket
stretches out to whip this length ball from well outside off to the right of long-on
pre_text: Last ball of the powerplay.

commentary: back of a length close to off stump, opens the bat face and steers to deep point
pre_text: Anrich Nortje. Slip in place with the field now going back.

commentary: hard length, angling across to finish on middle stump. Stays leg side of the ball and looks for the dabbed single towards point, but the ball stops close to the pitch and there's no single available
pre_text: Stays over the wicket to Axar.

commentary: length ball slanting across to off stump, steered to deep point with an open face
back of a length, angling in, looks to tuck it away but can't connect, hits the thigh pad
pre_text: SRIVENKATESH: "Boucher said in the Pre Match interview to Star Sports said the powerplay score would be 45 for 3"

commentary: again some steep bounce. Slower bouncer over the stumps, and it takes an age to reach Kohli but it gets up around neck high. Rolls his wrists over the pull to keep it down towards deep square leg
length ball on leg stump, clipped to deep midwicket
full, angled into leg stump from round the wicket, clipped to long-on
pre_text: Markram continues. How will India play him?

commentary: full on off stump, clipped to deep midwicket
pre_text: over the wicket to Kohli.

commentary: just clears deep midwicket. Takes the risk, but goes with the wind. Tossed up, angling in towards middle stump, turns a little too, but he gets a good stride in to slog-sweep against the turn and connect well enough
very full now, angling into middle stump, dug out into the off side
slows it down on off stump, goes for the slog-sweep again, drags it towards square leg off the bottom half of the bat
goes back to a length ball spinning in from outside off, punches with a straight bat to deep midwicket
goes back and punches a length ball down to long-off. Just outside off
pre_text: Maharaj returns. Feels like Axar doesn't have much of a choice but to go after him. First up it's Kohli though. Left-arm around.

commentary: uses the angle across the left-hander to almost force him to hit to deep point. Just back of a length too. Not much choice but to play the cut
pre_text: Stays round the wicket to Axar.

commentary: full on leg stump, gets forward to clip to long-on
looks to angle it away from Axar's hitting arc again, but doesn't succeed on this occasion. Just full enough, and not quite wide enough, and Axar can bring out the big slog-sweep over deep midwicket
flatter, mostly goes with the angle away from off stump, goes back and punches to short cover
nicely bowled. A bit of drift to accentuate the angle across, and Axar goes back and punches to forward square leg, meeting the ball just outside off
starts with a wide outside off. Looks to go flat and quick and away from the hitting arc, on the shorter side of a length. Ends up firing it too wide for the batter to attempt a shot
pre_text: Here's Tabraiz Shamsi. Left-arm over.

commentary: full on leg stump, clipped to long-on
quick length ball, turns from middle to off, gets forward to defend into the covers
pre_text: Over the wicket to Axar as well.

commentary: he's bowling a really good pace here. Axar isn't able to get onto the front foot quickly as this spins fairly sharply away from middle and off. Defended with the turn
quick, flat, turns from leg to middle and off. Stays back and clips towards deep midwicket

back of a length, turning down leg, clipped away to the left of the diving short fine leg fielder, and they hustle to try and get the second as deep backward square gets to the ball. Has to hurry, but the throw to the keeper's end isn't accurate enough to really make him sweat
tossed up outside off, and out comes the slog-sweep, along the ground to the left of deep midwicket. Again they hustle and take two, but they have to really push because Stubbs is electric
full length outside off, and a flat hack from Axar! Slower ball, skews off a leading edge, but short of deep third
pre_text:
Greetings. This has been a ding-dong opening gambit. Punch, counter-punch, regroup... more punches to come? You'd have to assume so!

Kohli, for all his endurance, made 14 from his first five balls, and 22 more from his next 24. Here's Jansen, the man he took down in the first over

commentary: pushed across the right-hander, but avoiding the slot length this time, Kohli rocks into a cut to deep point
back of a length, fenced down to short third
back of a length, Jansen mixing it up without being too full. Kohli swivels into a pull but doesn't connect cleanly on the leaping bounce
slower ball, back of a length, Axar adjusts well on the angle into off, and taps a late cut to deep third
fires in a loopier full length but that slides past the legs
leg-sided on the short ball, deflected off the hips
steps into the full length, and clipped to the on-side
flicked off the toes, out to square leg. Tight lines into the stumps from Shamsi
attempted slog-sweep, but this grips on a middle-and-leg line and turns past the flashing blade into the pads
on the back foot, turning into the legs, helped off the toes for another single
goes big, goes long! Heart in the mouth for a moment with Rabada tracking round from wide long-on, but that was fast and flat, and straight enough to beat the outstretched hand!
drags the length back, chopped up and over point, not a proper contact but into space once more. Axar is playing the innings of the final so far
full, on the toes, flicked uppishly out to deep midwicket
pre_text: Nortje is back

commentary: punched through the line, to long-off, making room to leg as Nortje follows him on the pads
angled bat on the back foot, Nortje hitting a good in-between length, patted to point
fuller length, squirted out to point on the drive, beats the diving point
short, down the leg side
beats the outside edge as Axar attempts to run a single down to deep third, but can't connect as the ball hops past his splice
back of a length once more, shovelled off the pads to deep square leg. Just five runs off a very tidy comeback over
round the wicket, into the arc, but what a shot! Axar holds his shape magnificently as the ball appears under his eyes, then lifts his hands up into the full length, high and mighty over long-on!
steps back and across, slams a firm cut/drive out to deep cover
gives it the charge, Rabada bangs in the short ball. Too short for the square leg umpire, but might keep him crease-bound

Is this a run-out or overthrows?! South Africa seem very sure it's the former! And it is! De Kock picks up an attempted flick off the legs from Kohli, swooping and shying at the far end! The ball beat Axar's bat by three inches, then deflected away to the rope at long-off! Huge, huge moment! Axar wanted the single, but Kohli had his back to him, and he couldn't get back in time!
full length, bottom-handed shovel to long-on
full length, outswing to the left-hander, big swing from Dube but he loses his shape a touch and inside-edges onto his pads
on the back foot, chopped away to cover. Ten off the over, but what an important wicket
Dube dumps it long! I think it's on him to keep the pedal to the metal. Sitting back in the crease, swinging up into the length ball, solid over long-on!
drags the length back, and nudged off the hips to backward square
punched into the on-side
pace off on the short ball, Kohli rolls his wrists into a delayed, controlled pull, to backward square
full toss, swinging into the pads at an awkward height as Dube looks to release his levers. Tucked into the leg side
skips to the pitch, big wind-up through a more expansive launch to leg, but he drags it a touch, on the bounce to deep midwicket
turning into the legs, can't work it square but finds enough of a gap
beauty! Drift, dip and turn, Dube is rather tentative, back in his crease and beaten past the outside edge
very full, Dube swings lustily, but under-edges the shot to short third
wider line, dragged hard into the leg side, but once again on the bounce to deep midwicket. Who will blink first in a key over?
swung furiously out through midwicket! Tossed up outside off, imparts huge power with his front foot thrust down the pitch, one bounce before the rope
clubbed hard through the line but only as far as long-on. That was a good over from South Africa's POV. Seam to close it out now
outside off, chopped to deep backward point for the single
pre_text:
Lengths by pacers so far, from S Rajesh
full and good length - 41 off 22
short and back of length - 17 off 23

commentary: back of a length, Kohli flicks up into the pull as Nortje takes a bit of pace off, the ball flips just out of de Kock's reach as he dives behind the stumps
back of a length again, thumped back through Nortje's tumbling followthrough, mopped up by mid-on
surprise fuller length, poked out to point for a diving take. Cover appeals for the crowd catch, but that was down into the crease
short again, rolls the wrists into the pull... out to deep midwicket. Kohli has his fifty... but he hasn't got a boundary since the fourth over
back of a length, carved away for a precious boundary! Dube made room well, shaping to the leg side to create the width that Nortje wasn't offering. Hitting with the breeze too. Quality
Kohli goes long at last! Length ball outside off, and that's what you want on this pitch. A full slap over long-on, not perfectly timed but cleared by a distance
pre_text: Rabada's back for his fourth

commentary: yorker, in at the toes, Kohli connects with a firm stab of the bat out to deep midwicket, and finds the space to get back for two
back of a length, uses the pace well, rolling the wrists as Rabada's slower ball arrives too straight. Hauled behind the square leg sweeper
fuller length, clipped up into the leg-side as Rabada follows his early movements
oops, a horrid full wide, that one slipped out of the hand. De Kock did well to prevent the boundary
wide yorker, that's what he was loading up, Dube chops down to deep third with a lusty swing outside off
yorker to finish, right into the blockhole, clipped on the up to the leg side, and the 150 comes up
Full length outswinger, Jansen reckon Kohli has nicked this, but he's overstepped! It was sent upstairs, then straight back down again for a free hit...
pre_text: It will be Jansen, SA keep the faith

commentary: free hit... swinging away, inside the tramlines, Kohli makes room to leg and almost swings himself off his feet, trying to make contact
full toss, on the pads, free runs! Maybe Markram shouldn't have kept the faith after all. Pretty poor ball at this crucial stage, whipped through backward square
back of a length, outside off, thumped down the ground, Markram almost rolls his ankle while intercepting, and they get  back for two
another slot ball, another slam-dunk! Outside off, in Kohli's arc, and if the first six was a bit of a mishit, this is utterly munched over wide midwicket!
drags the length back, swung in the air, down to wide long-on, and Kohli is done! It's been a significant knock, but is it the title-winner? All will be revealed
pre_text: Big two balls for Jansen, who is under the pump. A change of ball after that last launch
dismissal: V Kohli c Rabada b Jansen 76 (87m 59b 6x4 2x6) SR: 128.81

commentary: swings into the short ball, big top-edge over the keeper! 17 off the over as Jansen retreats with some pretty bruised figures
full length but too wide, Dube cocks his wrists and waits for the umpire to spread his arms
pre_text: Nortje, on the other hand, has conceded 17 in three overs... here he is to close things out

commentary: swung lustily off the toes, in the air out to deep midwicket. Full and fast, and couldn't time the contact
attempted yorker, comes out as a low full-toss, but at 144kph/89mph, that's hard to put away, thumped to mid-off
attempted wide yorker, misses his mark by a whisker, and clobbered past mid-on! Such a sweet contact, down the ground with raw power

belted hard through the full length, that was travelling seriously quickly and Miller at long-off does well to judge his take, sliding into the ball as it arrives with high velocity. A useful cameo, but a handy dot as well
dismissal: S Dube c Miller b Nortje 27 (32m 16b 3x4 1x6) SR: 168.75

commentary: wide line, full length, clubbed hard up and over point, but not totally nailed by Jaddu
huge swing through the full length, wide of off, a steepling leading edge, and a good diving take at mid-off. South Africa close it out well, but that is a hefty score on the board all the same
dismissal: RA Jadeja c Maharaj b Nortje 2 (1m 2b 0x4 0x6) SR: 100

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Hendricks, no run
commentary: fullish, a bit of swing in towards off stump, defended into the covers
pre_text: Hello, hello. Is this the last time Quinton de Kock is walking out to bat for South Africa? It would be some way to sign off if he wins this for them, and gives them that trophy they've craved for so, so, so long. Reeza Hendricks opens with him; he's had a quiet World Cup so far. Arshdeep Singh has the new ball for India. The target is 177. No slip. Fine leg and square leg are on the boundary. Left-arm over.

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Hendricks, no run
commentary: edged, but it doesn't carry. Slower ball, and it's the cutter nipping away off the track. Pitches outside off, on a length, and goes further away. Pushes at it without really moving his feet, and the edge bounces a foot or so before reaching Pant

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Hendricks, 1 leg bye
commentary: back of a length, straightens into Henrdicks after pitching outside leg. Misses the flick, rolls away to the left of Pant off the thigh pad

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to de Kock, no run
commentary: a bit of swing. Fullish length, angling in towards middle and swinging towards off, punched to midwicket
pre_text: De Kock on strike for the first time. Wind blowing towards his off side. Slip in place.

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to de Kock, 1 run
commentary: length ball close to off stump, chopped down to deep third
pre_text: Deep third and a squarish deep fine leg.

commentary: slower ball, looks to slant it away from Hendricks' reach, and maybe looking for the uppish drive, but he holds his shape, gets his head moving towards the ball, and reaches out to drive between backward point and cover point

short_text: Bumrah to de Kock, no run
commentary: good length, slanting across, and I don't think it did anything off the pitch necessarily. Kept going with the angle across, and QdK may have been playing for a bit of swing into him. Beaten while looking to drive on the up through mid-off
pre_text: Jasprit Bumrah. South Africa have 24 balls to negotiate from him. Over the wicket to QdK with fine leg and deep third back, and a slip.

short_text: Bumrah to de Kock, 1 leg bye
commentary: full on the pads, misses the flick and Pant, diving right, fumbles the deflection off the pad

has anyone bowled a better delivery in a T20 World Cup final? Wow. Reeza tends not to move his feet a great deal early on, and he gets out to the perfect outswinger. Perfect length to hit the top of off stump after angling in and veering away so, so late to beat the outside edge as Hendricks looks to defend with a straight bat. Beautiful. His front leg ended up planted in place, and his feet whrre unable to move thereafter, so he had to basically push his bat out in front of his boy to try and meet it, but a lot of batters may have been bowled by this ball even if they'd moved their feet

length ball, close to off stump, and Markram just stands tall and punches it away, letting it come to him, meeting it right under his eyes with a straight bat to send it flying to the right of backward point
pre_text: Aiden Markram is in at No. 3.

commentary: back of a length in the corridor, a hint of away shape, left alone

similar ball to the one that got Reeza, on a length, finishing top of off after a bit of late outswing, but Markram shows how to play it, getting his head right on top of the ball, getting his body moving into the ball, and defending into the covers

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to de Kock, 1 run
commentary: full, angling into middle stump, shows the full face and pushes to the right of mid-on
pre_text: Arshdeep continues.

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Markram, no run
commentary: slower ball, full, slanting away from off stump, reaches out with his hands and stabs it to backward point

got him, Markram has edged a big drive to the keeper! Wasn't a half-volley. On the fuller side of a length, well wide of off stump, the seam doesn't quite come out of the hand straight, and the ball doesn't swing back in. Just keeps going with the angle across, and Markram, going hard at it with a diagonal bat, gets a thick edge that carries at about ankle height to Pant, falling to his right
pre_text: 50th T20I for Chris Gaffaney, incidentally.
dismissal: AK Markram c †Pant b Arshdeep Singh 4 (4m 5b 1x4 0x6) SR: 80

commentary: again he angles a wide length ball across, and Stubbs drives with a roll of the wrists, out to the right of deep point
pre_text: Tristan Stubbs walks in at No. 4. Slip in place.

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to de Kock, no run
commentary: goes short now, angling down leg, and de Kock, looking to hook, is a little cramped for room. Misses, or did he get a little touch on this? Rishabh Pant thinks so, and India review the not-out decision. Was there a tiny nudge of glove on this? De Kock looks a little sheepish, but that's not too far from his usual expression. Nothing on Ultra Edge, and India lose their review
pre_text: akash: "I have opened cricinfo two times while watching match, each time SA has lost wickets. I will be doing it every five minutes now on "

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to de Kock, 1 run
commentary: slower ball again, fullish, angling in towards off stump. De Kock spots it, gets a stride forward to push to the right of long-on. Interesting how often he's gone off-pace with this new ball

puts it away in the gap, but was he looking to play it that fine. Bumrah angles a hard-length ball across de Kock, and he steers it away between slip and short third. Hit his bat somewhere between its middle and the top edge
full, angling across, driven to the right of mid-off
length ball angling in towards middle stump, clipped to deep square leg
pre_text: Round the wicket now.

commentary: fullish, angling into middle and leg, clipped to short midwicket
pre_text: Harish: "With Jansen slated to play at No.7, SA can't afford to lose any more wickets until 10th over to give themselves a good chance to win this."

commentary: slower ball from Bumrah this time. Fullish outside off, and Stubbs gets a nice stride into the ball to punch it to short cover
length ball angling into off stump, uses the angle nicely to clip it down to fine leg
steps across immediately to try and sweep this fine, but is struck on the pad by the inward-angling length ball. Struck outside the line
pre_text:
Axar. Left-arm around

Sunny G: "Is it something in the pitch that is making it harder to bat? Or just some good power play bowling from SA and Ind?" -- There's been juust a little hint of seam movement if you hit the pitch hard, but more often a bit of extra bounce. Good batting pitch, but not a belter.

commentary: nicely played. A touch short, perhaps a reaction to the attempted sweep off the last ball, and even though there isn't a lot of width, he times his back-cut perfectly to the left of short third
makes a bit of room to cut again, but a bit slower and straighter, slaps it to cover
down the track, too close to the pitch for an aggressive shot, punches down to long-off
angled across to finish just outside off, and de Kock creates extra room and slaps it away over the covers
pre_text: Stays round the wicket to de Kock.

commentary: back of a length, close to off stump, dabbed to short third
pre_text: Over the wicket now.

short_text: Kuldeep Yadav to de Kock, 1 run
commentary: flat, angled into the pads. Looks to squeeze any room QDK might have. Tucked to backward square leg
pre_text: Spin from both ends now. Kuldeep. Left-arm over.

commentary: clear intent from Stubbs here. Makes a lot of room, exposes all his stumps, and throws his bat at a middle-stump length ball. A bit of extra bounce, and the top edge clears backward point but slows down near thje boundary
clears his front leg again and Kuldeep goes fuller, on off stump, quite quick. Doesn't quite get all the way down on his knee, semi-slog-sweeps along the ground to long-on
again looks to clear his front leg and Kuldeep goes full to deny him elevation. Stump-to-stump line this time, driven to long-on

short_text: Kuldeep Yadav to de Kock, no run
commentary: steps out and can't get to the pitch of this ball outside off. Not much turn, stretches out and defends into the covers

short_text: Kuldeep Yadav to de Kock, FOUR
commentary: wrong'un, just back of a length, and it doesn't turn enough to deny de Kock room. Creates a bit more room and cuts it away between point and backward point. Was initially shaping for the reverse-sweep but didn't over-commit to that shot
back of a length, keeps going with the angle into the top of the stumps, makes room and chops to the off-side sweeper
pre_text: India made 45 for 3 in their powerplay, South Africa are 42 for 2. Axar continues, round the wicket to Stubbs.

commentary: very full on the stumps, denies elevation, makes room and drives to long-off
pre_text: Stays round the wicket to QDK.

commentary: shot. Lovely hockey swing there on the slog-sweep. Not full enough to deny elevation, but full enough to be in Stubbs' hitting arc for the slog-sweep on off stump. Hits it straight of deep midwicket, on the bounce
back of a length, finishes on off stump, makes room and punches to deep cover point

short_text: Patel to de Kock, no run
commentary: stays round the wicket, fires one at the pads, swept but without much power to short fine leg

short_text: Patel to de Kock, no run
commentary: similar line, a bit slower, through the sweep too early and he inside-edges into his pads

drilled. Superb, quick hands from Stubbs. Loops it up, wants to get it right up to squeeze the room for the drive, but his bat-swing is so quick and free, he steps out and drills it back between the stumps and the non-striker
full again, gets forward and clips to deep midwicket

short_text: Kuldeep Yadav to de Kock, 1 run
commentary: full at the pads, clipped to the left of short fine leg
hangs back to a length ball on leg stump, clips it towards deep midwicket

short_text: Kuldeep Yadav to de Kock, no run
commentary: wrong'un, looped up wide of off stump. Looks for the drive through the covers, hits the inside half of the bat and rolls back to the bowler

short_text: Kuldeep Yadav to de Kock, SIX
commentary: another wrong'un, but this is right in the slot, close to off stump, for Kuldeep to drop onto his back knee and slog-sweep waaaaay over the midwicket boundary and onto the solar-panelled roof of the stand. Hit that with such a fluid bat-swing. Brings up the 50 partnership, and these two are looking ominous now for India

so good from Stubbs. That was not an easy ball to slog-sweep, it was a touch short to play it comfortably, and started well outside off, but he stepped across, got low, and almost pulled it from there, to the left of the man at deep backward square leg
pre_text: Third over in a row for Axar.

commentary: makes room, slaps this leg-stump ball out to deep point
looks to reverse-sweep, inside-edges onto his pad
length ball angling in towards off stump, no real turn, makes room and chops to short third

Delhi Capitals gets Delhi Capitals. He'd stepped across once earlier this over to manufacture a boundary, but when he does so this time, Axar fires it full and at the stumps, and pretty much bowls him around his legs as he misses the sweep. Another big moment in a terrific, seesawing final
fired in at the pads, misses the flick and picks up a leg bye off the outside of his pad, into the backward square leg region
pre_text: Heinrich Klaasen. Just the man you want walking in in this situation, against this spin attack. How good are these two teams?

commentary: back of a length in the corridor, punched off the back foot and short cover dives right to stop it
pre_text:
Hardik Pandya. 

Anand: "The shot is not surprising from Stubbs. He has got a first-class triple ton. Takeaway is not to go crazy over "T20 specialists". Kudos to SA for picking him." -- He certainly has all the skills to play every format.

commentary: length ball angling into off stump, clipped to midwicket, who's stationed very straight, in line with the popping crease at the bowler's end
slower ball, into the pitch outside off. Stops on Klaasen who's initially looking for the cut. Ends up dragging it towards midwicket off the inside half of the bat

what a shot. Shows the small margins for error at this level. Another short slower ball into the pitch, but a bit more width on this occasion and he hops, gets on top of the bounce, and frees his arms to slap that all the way over the point boundary
pre_text: Third comes into the circle, midwicket drops back.

commentary: length ball angling into the stumps, clipped down to long-on. Looks like he's overstepped here.

miscued high in the air, and Pant gets under it behind the stumps, but it's a free-hit. On the fuller side of a length, and de Kock looks to swipe it over midwicket. Ends up hitting it behind him, almost vertically in the air
pre_text: Free-hit coming up. That was such a marginal no-ball. Heel juuuust on the front edge of the crease. Round the wicket now to de Kock.

commentary: shortish at the hip, paddle-pulled down to fine leg
on the back foot, clubbed out to deep point with a full swing of the bat
pre_text: Hello again. India were 75 for 3 at the halfway mark. South Africa just ahead, and they know what they have to do... this, as they say, is game on...

commentary: back of a length, but not by much, hauled with a cross-batted launch to deep midwicket, gets there on the bounce
pounded up into the length! Klaasen is so good at that stroke. Stepping into the full length, and breaking his wrists up and over long-off!
skids through faster and flatter outside off, cuffed to point
round the wicket, tapped off the pads with no great pace, but there's a long long chase into acres of space, and Jadeja has to make the ground himself
fired through flatter outside off, cut to deep point. A 12-run over keeps South Africa ticking along

short_text: Kuldeep Yadav to de Kock, 1 run
commentary: skimmies down the track, Kuldeep fizzes it out wider, QDK adjusts in a hurry and toe-ends to point with Pant lurking for the stumping

short_text: Kuldeep Yadav to Klaasen, no run
commentary: skids through on off stump, cut without power into the covers

unbelievable skill! Kuldeep fires out a wider line, back of a length with big turn away on the googly, Klaasen sits with his weight back in the crease, yet still manages to lift it high over extra cover. 100 up too
fired down the leg-side, swept hard behind square

short_text: Kuldeep Yadav to de Kock, no run
commentary: steps into the length, pushed into the covers

short_text: Kuldeep Yadav to de Kock, no run
commentary: top-spin on a wider line, QDK is lured into a loose cut and immediately grimaces as he just gets away with it. No damage done, this partnership endures
on the pads, tucked square for the single
pre_text: Back comes Arshdeep, with India rather keen for a breakthrough

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to de Kock, FOUR
commentary: back of a length, QDK rocks inside the line, and hoists it over fine leg! Using the angle across his body from the left-armer, with fine leg up in the ring. Free runs when you're that good!

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to de Kock, OUT
commentary: did he even notice the fielder! De Kock goes for the shot once more, rocking inside the line to the angle into his body, but Kuldeep has dropped back onto the rope, and barely needs to move! It was hit well, would have gone for six unlike the previous ball, but that's a giveaway after such a doughty innings
pre_text: Fine leg drops back...
dismissal: Q de Kock c Kuldeep Yadav b Arshdeep Singh 39 (54m 31b 4x4 1x6) SR: 125.8

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Miller, no run
commentary: good length ball, nipping back into the left-hander, inside-edged onto the pads
pre_text: It's Miller time... and the chase is very much on

commentary: on the toes, full length, nudged off the legs behind square
finds space in the covers and trots back for two more. A productive over in real terms, but Arshdeep bags the key wicket
looped up into the toes, clipped with the spin to deep midwicket, "two, two, two" is the call

short_text: Kuldeep Yadav to Miller, no run
commentary: back of a length, pace off outside off, Miller opens the face to flick to backward point
into position early for the sweep, hitting down on the full length outside off, picks off the single to deep midwicket
nurdled off the toes, out to backward square leg

back of a length, and finds the rope with the cut! A touch short, just outside off, and Miller's hit in front of square just kept eluding the fielder, who looked like he might have made it with a dive, but didn't get close
rocks back for the grandslam finish to the over! Kuldeep's figures get the Jansen treatment at the death, a touch too short and straight, and hoisted over deep midwicket!
steps deeper into his crease, lifted dismissively over the bowler's head! So good at hitting off the back foot! The power is preposterous
fired outside off, Klaasen doesn't flinch
wide again, tighter line but same result
has a flash with slightly flat feet, no contact
steps to the off side this time, and it's on the roof! 99 metres of pure muscle! Anticipated the wide line once more, moved effortlessly into position, and launched it!
it's close to a run a ball now! Axar has been India's player of the tournament, but Klaasen, deep in his crease again, belts violently on the up and over long-on!
steps into the length, hits into the wind! Violence and authority, Axar has nowhere to hide as Klaasen plants his front foot into the length and drills it through wide long-off!
width outside off, hacked over the covers, it's a massive over, and if South Africa don't believe now, they never will!
round the wicket, hard length angled into the left-hander, inside-edge past the stumps! The worm has turned...
back over the wicket, full length on the pads, tucked to midwicket. Singles, shockingly, will suffice. But that's a 23-ball fifty, the fastest in a final, from the mighty Klaasen
full and fast, thuds the pads, raucous appeal but that's clearly missing leg
yorker, so good! Klaasen digs down on the ball rather desperately, but crucially he digs it out
full on the pads, flicked with the angle, safely into space behind square. Another single, and that frankly is ample against India's dangerman

full length, Miller steps into the length outside off, and drives at short cover. A dot, but crucially, a blank as far as the wickets go. Bumrah has six balls left, and he's got to bowl them next over, surely

wide line, gets the nick! The break in play did the trick! Klaasen reached for the slam through the covers, very full length, but his feet were stuck in clay. He's livid with himself as he departs, but what a sensational knock!
pre_text: Where does Rohit turn now? To compound their problems, Pant is down with a knee niggle, though the breather might help his side. One partnership breaking ball, and see what they can salvage. Hardik is where India turn

commentary: steps into the length ball, outside off, a compact drive into the covers, and a raise of the hand to declare 'no run!'
wide line on the full length, solid bat through ball on the front foot from Jansen, guided down to deep third
tight line, on the pads, nudged to the on-side, and Miller takes the single. 100 balls gone, 20 to go...
full length, angled in at off stump, draws a tentative push into the leg side, but finds another single. That's ample at this stage
slow bouncer, Miller reads it well and settles for a controlled pull to square leg, rolling his wrists on the ball to keep the strike
snorter to start! Tight line from round the wicket, and that misses both the outside edge and the off stump by a whisker! Miller sliding to leg, then drawn back to the line like a magnet
pre_text: As expected, it's Bumrah or bust ... six balls, one wicket, two runs would be nice for India!

commentary: wicket-to-wicket pace, Miller settles for the full-faced block back down the line of off... two dots!
a touch more width this time, just back of a length, Miller flashes a drive out to deep cover and takes the single

sensational delivery! Jasprit Bumrah is the bowler from the Gods! Pace, angle, length, lift, Jansen plays the perfect defensive block, and is bowled through the gate as the ball flicks the top of his bails! This is too tense to function. Pass me an umbrella to gnaw!
pre_text: Three in the circle on the off side

commentary: so tight and full! Aggressive angled length, demanding a front-foot block
pre_text: Right. Two balls. Two dots would be just fine for South Africa. In fact, anything but a Miller run-out would do!

commentary: tapped into the covers off the full length, takes the single. Bumrah has delivered, ahem, one wicket and two runs, and even better, he's got Miller off strike

commentary: over the wicket, tight line and length, Maharaj presses back down the line, and it's another dot! It was a run a ball not so long ago... it's nearer two a ball now!
pre_text: Back comes Arshdeep, he's been magnificent today. What can he leave for the final over

pre_text: Third man inside the circle

commentary: Maharaj slides back and across, good contact on the pull up into the leg-side, one bounce to deep midwicket. There is the single
pre_text: It is now two runs a ball. Miller has to get back on strike somehow

commentary: hoisted across the line, out to midwicket! Not perfect contact on a forced pull, not quite short enough to clobber. But crucially he's back for the second
pre_text: How does Miller play this? A boundary or two would be nice, but getting on strike for the 20th is the priority

commentary: yorker, fired in at the left-hander's toes, inside-edged for the single to backward square

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Maharaj, no run
commentary: beautiful wide yorker! Maharaj toe-ends his drive, back out of the length, Arshdeep leaps to gather, and claws down the dot ball!
pre_text: A shot to nothing for Maharaj now, like Archer in the 2019 final. Boundary or bust...

commentary: wide full toss flogged down the ground for the most sensational catch you can ever imagine! That is a moment for the ages, Miller connected well, but not well enough to take Suryakumar Yadav out of the equation. He hurtled round from wide long-off, clawed down the ball with barely two hands, toppling over the rope as he went, kept his feet inside the rope... and lobbed the ball back into play, and into his own cool-as-cucumber hands!
